video.title: If People Pay for This, Your Idea Will Work Too

summary: Chris Koerner and a co-host brainstorm business ideas built around the theme that people will pay for almost anything, and that ego stops people from doing weird, attention-getting things. Ideas include novelty competition events (horse haircut show, Excel esports, vibe-coding competitions, survival challenges), a plaque-selling service triggered by magazine features, a YouTube-to-print-magazine service, and quirky marketing stunts such as a realtor 'ghost free guarantee'. Evidence is mostly brainstorming and second-hand anecdotes, with few verified numbers. Key takeaway: memorable, talk-worthy content or events can create demand and customers in otherwise boring niches.

speakers.name: Brandon
speakers.description: Co-host, addressed by name at the end

ideas.name: Novelty competition events (horse hair show)
ideas.one_liner: Ticketed niche competition event with entry fees, spectator tickets and sponsor booths, based on a viral horse-haircut show.
ideas.business_model: Ticket sales, competitor entry fees, sponsor booths
ideas.customer: Horse owners, spectators, sponsors, and the barbers who organise it
ideas.problem: Niche communities lack a fun gathering and organisers lack customer attention
ideas.offer: Live competition event where horses with intricate shaved patterns are judged

pricing.notes: Reported from a viral Instagram video, second-hand.

acquisition_channels.details: Viral Instagram video of the shaved horse promoted the event

ideas.delivery: Physical in-person event run by organiser (reportedly a barber) in Clovis, California.

acquisition.how: Short-form video content can be produced and posted largely by agents.

onboarding.how: Ticketing and registration platforms handle sign-ups.

delivery.how: Physical event needing venue, staff and judging.

support.how: Day-of logistics need humans; pre-event queries can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK with event licensing, insurance and animal welfare considerations.

quotes.text: They're selling general admission tickets for $30. They're selling, you know, you could admit your horse to be judged and graded for $110.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Free marketing-stunt events for local service businesses
ideas.one_liner: Local businesses run fun free competitions (dirty car speed clean, accountant tax race) to generate attention and customers.
ideas.business_model: Free event as marketing, customers acquired from content and attention
ideas.customer: Local service businesses such as window cleaners and accountants
ideas.problem: Boring businesses struggle to get attention
ideas.offer: Creative public events and content that get eyeballs

acquisition_channels.details: Event footage as content to attract customers

ideas.delivery: Business owner performs the stunt in person and films it.

acquisition.how: Content editing and posting can be automated but the stunt needs humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same in the UK.

quotes.text: there's no such thing as a boring business. There's only boring content.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Excel esports / financial modeling competitions
ideas.one_liner: Livestreamed spreadsheet competitions with entry fees, spectators and software-company sponsors.
ideas.customer: Finance and Excel enthusiasts, sponsors such as Microsoft, Notion and Airtable

acquisition_channels.details: Livestreams; one championship reportedly aired on ESPN2

acquisition.how: Content and community marketing can be agent-assisted.

quotes.text: There's the financial modeling world cup, which is a real thing. People live stream their screens.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Vibe-coding live competition
ideas.one_liner: Livestreamed competition where non-coders build an app (e.g. golf score tracker) with AI tools in 60 minutes, graded on set categories.
ideas.business_model: Competitor entry fees and spectator tickets, optional platform sponsorship
ideas.customer: Non-coder vibe coders/marketers as competitors; spectators; AI app-builder platforms as sponsors
ideas.offer: Nine-person grid screen-share contest with live commentator, judged on UI, design, database, ease of use; prize e.g. $5,000 or half the door pot

pricing.notes: Hypothetical; winner gets half of door fees.

acquisition_channels.details: Ask Lovable, Bolt, FlutterFlow, Replit to each send one competitor

ideas.delivery: Google Meet/stream with screen-sharing and a live commentator.
unit_economics_claims: $20 entry x 9 competitors, $5 per spectator, winner takes half of door

acquisition.how: Social posting and outreach to platforms (limited companies) is automatable.

risks: Prize pot legality/gambling-like structures to check

quotes.text: It's like $5 to spectate and the coders, the five marketers, they pay $20 as an entry fee.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Most Dangerous Game paintball race
ideas.one_liner: Pay-to-enter paintball race where racers try to reach a hidden-start finish line without being hit; organiser keeps the difference.
ideas.business_model: Entry fees into pot, organiser takes margin
ideas.customer: Teens and friends obsessed with the story

pricing.notes: First racer to finish unhit gets half the pot; shooters get pot per hit; organiser takes the difference.

ideas.delivery: In-person physical event run by organiser.

uk_applicability.notes: Needs venue, insurance and waivers; safety regulation.

quotes.text: whoever the first racer is to get to the end without getting hit gets half the pot. The shooters get the pot of each person they hit and then I would just take the difference.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Survival challenge (survivalbet.com concept)
ideas.one_liner: Premium wilderness survival competition for everyday men after a crash course, priced around $3,000.
ideas.customer: Adventure-seeking men wanting a do-hard-things experience
ideas.problem: Desire to test self-reliance without phones
ideas.offer: Multi-day wilderness survival experience with a 24-hour training crash course and predetermined judging

pricing.notes: Idea only; needs 50-500 acres and waivers.

ideas.delivery: In-person on rented/borrowed land with training and waivers.

uk_applicability.notes: Works with changes; UK land is limited and needs insurance and safety compliance.

quotes.text: it's going to cost like $3,000 to do it. Yeah. And you just need someone that can rent or borrow or steal or own 50 to 500 acres of land
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Behind-the-scenes content for professional services
ideas.one_liner: Lawyers, accountants and home service firms post behind-the-scenes stories and insights instead of only before/after content.
ideas.business_model: Content marketing to drive client acquisition
ideas.customer: Small businesses, lawyers, accountants, home service companies
ideas.problem: Samey content that doesn't get attention
ideas.offer: Behind-the-curtain content, screen-recorded insights and stories

acquisition.how: Editing and posting automatable; raw material needs owner.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same; mind client confidentiality.

quotes.text: Show behind the scenes content. If you're a lawyer and you have a tough case, you know, bleep out the names of the case
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: That's Great News plaque service
ideas.one_liner: Company emails people featured in alumni magazines offering to sell a plaque of the article; competitor idea to replicate for online articles.
ideas.business_model: One-off physical product sales via personalised outreach
ideas.customer: People featured in alumni magazines or online articles
ideas.problem: Pride in being featured with no way to commemorate it
ideas.offer: Plaque with the article page under plexiglass

acquisition_channels.details: Subscribe to alumni magazines, find featured people, Google their email, send personalised-looking email with disclaimer of no affiliation

acquisition.how: Cold email to individuals is restricted under UK PECR; scraping and finding emails raises GDPR issues.

delivery.how: Print-on-demand and fulfilment can be outsourced.

uk_applicability.notes: Unsolicited emails to individuals breach PECR; would need an inbound or consent route.

quotes.text: we are not associated with the University of Alabama in any way.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: YouTube-to-print-magazine service
ideas.one_liner: Turn a creator's YouTube tutorials into a physical magazine, automated by an app that takes a video URL and outputs a magazine.
ideas.business_model: Subscription magazine, revenue share with creator
ideas.customer: YouTube creators with large audiences, and their fans
ideas.problem: Audiences want physical content in an increasingly online world; creators want another revenue stream
ideas.offer: Quarterly magazine from creator content; creator promotes it and platform keeps 20%

pricing.notes: Cost about $2 per issue proposed; 20% off the top.

acquisition_channels.details: Pitch large creators such as Epic Gardening, which has 4 million YouTube subscribers on one channel
Creator promotes via weekly email and midroll ad

ideas.delivery: Auto-generated layout from video URL, printed and mailed by print partner.

acquisition.how: Outreach to creators is B2B and partly automatable, but deals need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK using UK print partners.

quotes.text: he has a $7 million a year business repurposing their YouTube tutorials into physical magazine.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: you'll send 12 bucks a quarter and your cost is only going to be two bucks to me.
quotes.speaker: Brandon

ideas.name: Ghost free guarantee for realtors
ideas.one_liner: Realtor or certifying body brands a tongue-in-cheek 'ghost free guarantee' badge for viral local PR.
ideas.business_model: Marketing stunt; possible certification seal fee

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ads to home shoppers in one city with high spend
Badge in Instagram, TikTok, YouTube videos

acquisition.how: Paid ads and content are automatable.

uk_applicability.notes: Works; avoid misleading claims under UK advertising rules, though clearly humorous.

quotes.text: Make sure everyone knows that you certified there are zero ghosts in that home.
quotes.speaker: Brandon

ideas.name: Weird flavour frozen yogurt stunt
ideas.one_liner: Odd product to bring people in and get them talking, inspired by Nathan For You.

tactics.name: Pay-to-play competition pot structure
steps: Charge competitors an entry fee ($20-40) so they take it seriously
Give winner half of the door fees to incentivise inviting friends and family
Limit to nine competitors in a 3x3 screen grid
Use a 60-minute clock graded on predetermined categories

quote.text: the winner gets like half of the pot, like half of the door fees.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Creator magazine revenue share
steps: Approach a creator with a large audience
Offer to produce and fulfil the magazine at about $2 per issue
Creator sells at $12 per quarter and promotes via weekly email and midroll

quote.text: I'll do a mag. It'll be a magazine.
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Bottom-up demand creation
steps: Get friends and family to repeatedly ask retailers or realtors for the product
Pitch the retailer once enquiries build
Or target home shoppers on Facebook within one city with heavy ad spend

quote.text: They just asked all their friends and family to call up all the J C Penney every day
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Trigger-based personalised outreach
steps: Monitor publications for features of individuals
Send a personalised-looking offer shortly after publication

warnings.warning: Survival competitions need waivers to avoid lawsuits if someone is hurt.

quote.text: you've got to sign waiverss at the yin-yang. You don't want people to sue you if someone gets sick.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Finding sponsors adds friction that stops people launching events.

quote.text: that's just another level of friction to prevent anyone from launching it, myself included
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The plaque company's outreach can look like an official gift, which is misleading, and it relies on a disclaimer in fine print.

lessons.lesson: Ego and fear of looking stupid stop people from doing attention-getting marketing that could make money.

quote.text: how much pride and ego prevents us from making more money.
quote.speaker: Brandon

lessons.lesson: There are no boring businesses, only boring content; creative events and stories get attention in dull niches.

quote.text: there's no such thing as a boring business. There's only boring content.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Marketing stunts do not need to be good ideas, just talk-worthy.

quote.text: It doesn't need to be a good idea. It just needs to get people talking.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: If a strange niche has paying customers, it is evidence that almost any passion niche can monetise; find analogues in your own area.
Plug into existing audiences with a revenue-share product instead of building your own audience.
As the world gets more digital, physical products like print magazines gain value.

quote.text: the more AI takes over, the more we're online, the more we want a physical magazine.
quote.speaker: Brandon

lessons.lesson: Personalised, trigger-based outreach tied to a moment of pride converts well.
Entry fees, even nominal, increase participant commitment.

evidence_quality.rationale: Brainstorm-style conversation; figures are second-hand, hypothetical or guesses, and most ideas are untested. Only the host's high-school paintball events are first-hand and unquantified.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes his newsletter and podcast (tkopod.com); no product sold.
